limitations: Category shares are conditional on recorded errors, not all samples. The supplied table excerpt does not quantify all listed criteria, and this distribution is not transferable as a local mix without validation.

source_title: Applying Lean methodologies reduces ED laboratory turnaround times
locator: Abstract, Methods and Results; full-text sections listed as Introduction, Methods, Results and Limitations
source_setting: Massachusetts General Hospital teaching-hospital emergency department and laboratory, Boston, Massachusetts
source_period: Prospective before-after intervention; exact observation dates and per-test counts not available in accessible article abstract
source_n: Six ED tests; exact test counts not stated in accessible abstract
quantity: Observed median collection-to-result TAT before and after workflow redesign
unit: minutes (medians; reduction values reported with 99% confidence intervals)
source_evidence_basis: Prospective before-after study reports median collection-to-result turnaround. Lean sample-flow reorganization without added resources reduced troponin T from 86 to 53 minutes (33-minute decrease; 99% CI 30-35) and urine sedimentation from 117 to 29 minutes (88-minute decrease; 99% CI 87-90).
limitations: Single teaching ED, intervention study, six selected tests; not randomized. Accessible abstract does not expose sample counts or exact dates. Results describe medians and must not be treated as a service-time distribution.
inferred_scenario_use: Separate collection, transport, accession, analysis, reflex-test, and result-report stages; reflex testing can add a second queue. Use medians only as external plausibility checks, not as a fitted distribution or RWJ target.

source_title: Improving Emergency Department Flow: Reducing Turnaround Time for Emergent CT Scans
locator: Abstract; Methods, intervention periods; Results; Discussion (schedule-ahead transport and order workflow)
source_setting: Large academic medical center adult emergency department, approximately 100,000 annual visits
source_period: Pre: July 1, 2015-March 1, 2016; post: July 1, 2017-March 1, 2018; intervention developed July 2016-July 2017
source_n: 10,063 CT orders in the eight-month pre-period; post-period order volume increased 13.8%; exact post count not stated in accessible text
source_evidence_basis: The observed baseline order-to-final-report TAT averaged 5.9 h (median 4.2 h) for 10,063 CT orders; an intervention bundle reduced TAT by 1.2 h in the corresponding post period despite 13.8% more orders (p<0.0001). The workflow crosses ED, transport, CT, and radiology handoffs; documented changes included communication, visual analytics, automation, education, and schedule-ahead transport to avoid batching transport requests.
limitations: Direct PubMed Central article access returned a verification wall, and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500 in this session. The values and workflow summary remain based on indexed article text pending direct primary-text inspection. Single-center bundled QI intervention; individual component effects cannot be isolated. The reported mean and median are not distributions.
inferred_scenario_use: Model imaging as order/protocoling, patient preparation, transport queue, scanner queue/acquisition, interpretation, preliminary/final report, with explicit handoffs and prioritization. Do not infer stage distributions from overall mean or median.

source_title: Improving Emergency Department radiology transportation time: a successful implementation of lean methodology
locator: Abstract; Methods, Study setting and population and revised process; Results
source_setting: American University of Beirut Medical Center academic urban ED; approximately 49,000 annual visits; on-site ED radiography room
source_period: Six months pre versus six months post, separated by one-month washout
source_n: 6,186 radiographs pre-intervention and 4,879 post-intervention; all ED plain-film patients during six-month comparison periods
quantity: Observed mean order-to-transport-completion time for plain radiography
source_evidence_basis: Original full-text XML: order-processing-to-study-completion mean TAT fell from 22.89±22.05 to 9.87±15.05 min (p<0.0001); 71.6% versus 32.3% completed within 10 min. Cohort sizes were 6,186 pre and 4,879 post radiographs. Changes included a pending-request dashboard and peak-hours dedicated transporter; preliminary resident reads and final attending reads were separate.
limitations: Plain radiography in one ED with an on-site suite; intervention included a dedicated transporter during peak hours. Not CT/MRI scheduling. Mean, SD and threshold share do not fully specify a distribution.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent transport request queue and transporter availability separately from imaging-room capacity; account for local modality, acuity, preparation, and staffing before applying any timing. Include preliminary and final reporting as distinct events.

source_title: Massive Transfusion Protocols: The Role of Aggressive Resuscitation Versus Product Ratio in Mortality Reduction
locator: Methods, cohort periods and time-to-product definition; Table 3; Results
source_setting: Stanford University Medical Center, county-designated ACS-verified Level I trauma center; trauma patients admitted through ED and receiving at least 10 PRBC units in first 24 h
source_n: 40 eligible pre-MTP and 37 eligible post-MTP patients; 4,223 and 4,414 trauma activations respectively
quantity: Mean minutes from patient presentation to first documented patient-specific crossmatched product transfused
source_evidence_basis: Observed retrospective cohort comparison associated MTP introduction with shorter mean time to first documented crossmatched product: RBC 115 to 71 min, plasma 254 to 169 min, platelets 418 to 241 min. Four uncrossmatched RBC units were already available at major trauma activations before and after; the defined endpoint concerns subsequent patient-specific crossmatched products. MTP also specified communication and system flow improvements.
limitations: Small, highly selected massive-transfusion trauma cohorts and nonrandomized protocol-era comparison. These are means from arrival to transfused product, not blood-bank preparation or release service times and not times for all ED patients.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent emergency release and subsequent patient-specific compatibility workflows as separate paths; MTP activation coordinates blood bank, trauma, and clinical teams and repeated product cycles. Do not use these cohort means as generic per-unit processing times.

source_title: Experience with uncrossmatched blood refrigerator in emergency department
source_setting: 945-bed ACS-verified Level I trauma center and tertiary center; adult ED patients receiving uncrossmatched RBCs from ED refrigerator
quantity: Observed emergency refrigerator blood use and activation counts
unit: patients, percent, units; median units per patient
source_evidence_basis: Original full-text XML: 158 adult ED patients received uncrossmatched RBC from the refrigerator; 140 were trauma patients, 37 received massive transfusion, and 89 had MTP activated. The study did not report request-to-issue time.
limitations: Single Level I trauma center; excludes patients who died in first 24 hours from its appropriateness subgroup analysis, and the study did not measure request-to-issue minutes. The authors used a study-specific proxy definition for potentially inappropriate transfusion.
inferred_scenario_use: Blood-bank model may include controlled ED emergency-stock location, issue/traceability, replenishment and compatibility follow-up, alongside central blood-bank MTP workflow. These counts describe one center and cannot establish RWJ stock levels or demand rates.

source_period: Workflow described for study conducted January-December 2018
source_n: Not a distinct numerical outcome; process description within study of 113,817 samples
value: collection by clinical or laboratory staff
source_evidence_basis: Original journal PDF, Methods: samples were sorted at reception, problems entered in a manual log, and rejection criteria covered identity/request, container, quantity, hemolysis/clot, transport, closure, and transit delay.
limitations: This is one hospital's process description and does not specify universal acceptance standards, response times, recollection service levels, or electronic tracking. Not verified as RWJ policy.
inferred_scenario_use: Use a rejection branch that records reason, notification, recollection request and repeat transport, so a rejected specimen does not silently become a result. Obtain local critical-sample exceptions and escalation policies before operationalizing.
